review_method.visual_basis: Direct inspection of the local Top-100 asset on 2026-08-05.
review_method.context_basis: Caption extracted from the supplied Top-100 workbook.
review_method.boundary: Caption context never substitutes for visual inspection; no factual claim inside the source post is treated as verified by this record.

source_context.creator: Not reliably extracted from the supplied workbook; inspect post or visible asset before attribution.
source_context.caption_hook: The Algorithm Insights Report 2026 is built on 1.3M+ posts and 80,000+ profiles.
caption_argument_segments: The Algorithm Insights Report 2026 is built on 1.3M+ posts and 80,000+ profiles. It tells you what mistakes to avoid. Where each format breaks. How to get the most out of it. But it doesn't tell you which formats to use.
That part is yours. Every creator builds their own mix based on strengths, goals, and what they actually enjoy making.

And before anyone says "the algorithm doesn't matter" I double dare you to publish a 50-slide carousel. A 12-minute video. A short post with an external link aimed at conversion. Then come back and tell me the algorithm…
It does. The report shows you the guardrails. But it's only you decide what to drive inside them.
Here's how I use (or ignore) the 8 formats right now:
𝗗𝗼𝗰𝘂𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 → 𝗺𝘆 𝗳𝗮𝘃𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗲, 𝗻𝗼 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁. Educational content, process breakdowns, authority pieces. Under 10 slides, short copy. The report says 9.2 is the sweet spot. I'm aligned here.
observed_performance_context: Included in Tiger’s intentionally curated Top-100 reference set.
unknowns: Original post-level analytics unless separately captured.
Independent validation of factual or numerical claims within the source post.

reader_situation.topic_selection_boundary: The record does not select a future topic, audience, factual claim or post angle.

attention_physics.thumbnail_read_0_3_seconds: The asset’s first-frame promise is carried by Content-format metric tile grid.
attention_physics.comprehension_3_10_seconds: The reader follows the category groups, repeated entries, one shared legend or hierarchy to understand the structure without reading the full caption.
attention_physics.value_exchange_10_30_seconds: Compress a broad landscape of people, companies, tools or signals into a navigable overview.
attention_physics.identity_or_curiosity_trigger: market opacity; choice overload; need for orientation at scale
attention_physics.promise_proved_by_visual: The visual’s proof mechanism is Content-format metric tile grid.

visual_forensics.composition_and_grid: category groups; repeated entries; one shared legend or hierarchy; visible scope and provenance
visual_forensics.hierarchy: The visible promise and primary structure carry the first read; supporting detail is subordinate.
visual_forensics.typography: Assessed through the asset’s visible hierarchy; retain its function, not its source typeface or distinctive expression.
visual_forensics.colour_material_and_contrast: Use only as a meaning-bearing support to hierarchy and grouping; source palette is not a transferable requirement.
visual_forensics.imagery_role: Imagery supports the mechanism: Content-format metric tile grid.
visual_forensics.density_and_pacing: Fast first-frame orientation, then modular deep reading; the reader may exit after the promise or continue to the usable detail.
craft_observations: Reusable atom: One central numerical anchor with scannable tiles
The source’s visual identity, typography and precise layout remain non-transferable.

content_mechanics.primary_cognitive_job: Compress a broad landscape of people, companies, tools or signals into a navigable overview.
content_mechanics.compression_method: category groups; repeated entries; one shared legend or hierarchy; visible scope and provenance
content_mechanics.reader_payoff: Compress a broad landscape of people, companies, tools or signals into a navigable overview.
content_mechanics.caption_to_visual_choreography: State inclusion criteria, provenance, date sensitivity and what the landscape is not claiming.

mechanism_fingerprint.primary_cognitive_job: Compress a broad landscape of people, companies, tools or signals into a navigable overview.
use_when: The collection has a defensible scope and grouping logic.
The reader gains orientation from seeing the landscape together.
Sources, dates and exclusions can be named.
do_not_use_when: The map creates an implied ranking without evidence.
Entries are incomplete but presented as exhaustive.
The reader needs a focused decision rather than an overview.
mechanism_fingerprint.topic_selection_boundary: This mechanism chooses no topic. Opportunity selection occurs before reference retrieval and recombination.

transferable_atoms: One central numerical anchor with scannable tiles
recombination.reverse_build_specification: When a chosen opportunity requires landscape orientation, group a bounded set by one clear taxonomy, declare the scope and source basis, and make the reader’s next comparison possible. Do not disguise an unverified list as market truth.
required_original_inputs: A chosen reader tension with real relevance.
Correct logic, process or sourced evidence proportionate to the selected claim.
An original visual object/scene/interface that proves the chosen promise.
A caption that adds a different layer of value from the visual.
anti_copy_boundary: source creator identity, brand assets and distinctive composition
any source claim not independently supportable
recombination.falsification_question: After seeing an original execution, can a target reader identify the intended compress a broad landscape of people, companies, tools or signals into a navigable overview. without relying on the caption?
